source.title: How LLM Task-Adaptation Reshapes Alignment: A Multi-dimensional Study of Behavioral and Representational Drift
source.authors: James Elcock; William F. Shen; Xin-Chi Qiu; N. Lane

page_placements.theme: Refusal direction and refusal behaviour under fine-tuning, quantization and uncensoring: drift, compression and dissociation

record.tranche_reason: The study uses contrastive residual-stream concept directions, including the cited refusal prompt-pair protocol, to monitor representational drift during task adaptation. It does not intervene on the direction to test whether it causes refusal.
record.gate_note: The study measures refusal-related direction separation and its association with behavioral drift, and reports a behavioral change in jailbreak refusal. It does not ablate or add the direction, make a weight edit based on it, test an attack that suppresses it, or test the other specified mechanisms. These results do not directly test any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study takes the Arditi et al. prompt-pair difference-in-means protocol as a monitoring tool. It measures how far apart harmful and harmless cluster means sit at one AUC-selected layer before and after SFT, KL-SFT and RLVR, and correlates that shift with behavioural drift (r=+0.81). It never ablates, adds or weight-edits the direction, tests no attack that suppresses it, and makes no comparison of single versus multiple directions, harm versus refusal, transfer, or reasoning models. Fine-tuning already-aligned models and measuring cluster separation does not test whether one removable direction exists (V7). No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that task adaptation shifts alignment unevenly: SFT causes the most drift, RLVR little, and KL-SFT sits in between. Residual-stream concept directions, refusal included, track the behavioural drift, which suggests representation-level monitoring. They make no causal claim about a refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a refusal prompt-pair contrastive protocol attributed to Arditi et al. and difference-in-means concept directions, but measures separation at a selected layer after task adaptation rather than ablating or adding a direction across layers and positions. The study is a task-adaptation drift analysis, not a causal refusal-direction test.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by adaptation method, task, model, concept, checkpoint, and KL coefficient; the authors report model- and metric-specific changes and use model- and concept-specific layers.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT compresses the separation of the refusal difference-in-means direction. RLVR largely preserves it, and KL-SFT partially restores it (0.87 at β=0.05 to 0.92 at higher β, Qwen2.5-3B MATH).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task fine-tuning of aligned models can compress the harmful/harmless separation along the refusal direction, depending on the adaptation method.

fits_no_version.finding: Across checkpoints, the shift in refusal-direction separation correlates with behavioural refusal drift (r=+0.81, 95% CI [+0.54,+0.92]).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the refusal direction's separation tracks refusal behaviour under fine-tuning (correlational).

fits_no_version.finding: RLVR improves jailbreak refusal relative to the instruct baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RLVR task adaptation can improve jailbreak robustness.

record.problems: Training runs are single-seed. The refusal representation plot does not provide exact text-readable values for the aggregate SFT and RLVR conditions, and the reported refusal-direction correlation is observational rather than causal. The study is limited to 1.7B–8B models from two model families.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction to remove refusal, adding it to induce refusal, and whether other abilities are kept.
Turning the ablation into a weight edit (abliteration).
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Single direction versus affine, cone or multi-direction accounts.
Separating the harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base to instruct.
Whether the training regime determines that one removable direction exists. Only the separation after downstream fine-tuning is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The direction is used only as a measurement tool, at a single selected layer and the final input token. Runs are single-seed. Models are 1.7B–8B from two families.

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition of the refusal direction; no test of refusal removal, harmless-request refusal induction, or preservation of other abilities under such an intervention.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration test.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, base and instruct models, or model variants.
The study adapts already aligned models for downstream tasks; it does not vary how or when refusal is trained to test whether a removable direction forms.
No reasoning-model test of the single-direction refusal claim.

relation.reason: It extracts the refusal direction with Arditi et al.'s protocol and uses it as a tool, without testing whether the direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: The study uses the Arditi prompt-pair difference-in-means direction only as a monitoring measure (norm ratio of cluster-mean separation at an AUC-selected layer) and correlates it with behaviour. It has no ablation, addition or transfer test, so no version is tested.

source_check.notes: KL-SFT was trained only on Qwen2.5-3B and Llama3.2-3B (Table 2), so Figure 5's KL-SFT bars, and possibly the whole figure, cover at most those models. The ratio compares the norm of the mean difference, not the direction, so it says nothing on whether the direction transfers (V6). The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate.

statements.correction: SFT compresses several concept directions, with significant changes for refusal; RLVR largely preserves them (across models, Figure 5, refusal values figure-only). Qwen2.5-3B MATH KL-SFT: refusal ratio 0.87 at beta=0.05, 0.92 at higher beta. Refusal concept shift vs behavioural drift across trained SFT/KL-SFT/RLVR checkpoints and models: r=+0.81, 95% CI [+0.54,+0.92], Holm-significant.
statements.problem: The '(Qwen2.5-3B, MATH)' scope fits only the KL-SFT example. SFT compression and RLVR preservation of refusal are stated across models, refusal values appear only in a figure, and Figure 5 does not name its models.
